yell at: shout at someone in an angry way
typical: yell at sb. NOT for: speaking quietly.
yet: introduces something that contrasts with or surprises you after what was just said
typical: formal and written, joins clauses or starts a sentence. NOT for: time (see the other function).
It was cold, yet we enjoyed the walk.
He is rich, yet he never spends money.
The plan was simple, yet it failed.
means until now, with something expected later
typical: with negatives and questions in present perfect: not yet, yet? NOT for: contrast.
The results are not ready yet.
